mcqs.why: The motion of particles can be translational, vibrational or rotational, or a combination of these; the nature of the motion depends on the state of matter.

mcqs.q: The force of attraction between the particles of matter is greater when:
options: The separation between the particles is smaller
The separation between the particles is larger
The temperature of the matter is higher
mcqs.why: Postulate (c): the particles of matter attract each other, and this force depends on the separation between the particles: the smaller the separation, the greater the force of attraction.

mcqs.q: On cooling, steam changes back into:
options: Water, and then into ice on further cooling
mcqs.why: On cooling, steam changes back into water and then into ice, reversing the changes that heating produced.

mcqs.q: The particles of matter cannot be seen because they are:
options: Always moving too fast to be seen
Extremely small and not visible to the naked eye
mcqs.why: Matter consists of extremely small particles called atoms, molecules or ions, and these particles are not visible to the naked eye.

lessons.title: Solid, Liquid and Gas
lessons.notes_html:
The different states of matter can be explained on the basis of the particle theory of matter.

Solid

In a solid, the particles are very closely packed, in a regular pattern in most solids (crystalline solids); particles are also very closely packed in non-crystalline solids. For this reason solids have a high density. Strong forces of attraction hold the particles close together: they cannot be further compressed. The particles can vibrate only about their equilibrium position and cannot make any translation or rotation, so the particles of a solid possess only vibrational kinetic energy. A solid has a definite shape and volume.

Liquid

When a solid is heated it melts into its liquid form: on heating, the binding force between the particles of the solid becomes slightly weak. In a liquid, the separation between two particles is large compared to a solid, and for this reason the density of most liquids (except mercury) is less than that of solids. The particles of a liquid are arranged randomly; they can move freely from one part of the liquid to another but are confined to the boundary of the container. A liquid has a definite volume but no definite shape: it acquires the shape of its container, so a liquid can flow. A liquid cannot be compressed. A liquid possesses translational and vibrational kinetic energies.

Gas

The separation between the particles of a gas is very large compared to the size of the particles, which results in an extremely low density of gases compared to solids and liquids. The forces of attraction between the particles of a gas are negligible due to their large separation. The particles of a gas move randomly and in all directions within the boundary of the container; they move at high speeds and may spin at elevated temperature, so a gas can possess translational, vibrational and rotational kinetic energies, depending on its temperature. The particles of the gas often collide with one another and with the walls of the container: the forces exerted by the particles during these collisions produce the pressure of the gas. As the separation between particles is quite large, a gas can be compressed. Unlike the particles of a solid or liquid, gas particles do not occupy a fixed volume and quickly fill any available space.

Note: the available copy of the book ends here, at book page 234. The remaining sections of this unit (Plasma; Motion of Particles and Temperature; Temperature and Heat; Thermometers and their scales) and Units 13 and 14 are not included in these notes.

Key Points

  • Matter is made of atoms, molecules or ions, which are in constant motion.
  • The force of attraction between particles is greater when the separation is smaller.
  • Solid: closely packed particles, only vibrational energy, definite shape and volume.
  • Liquid: random particles, definite volume but no definite shape; it flows.
  • Gas: very large separations, negligible attraction, fills any space, and can be compressed.

mcqs.q: In a solid, the particles are:
options: Very far apart and randomly arranged
Very closely packed, in a regular pattern in most solids
Free to move throughout the container
Arranged with large gaps between them
mcqs.why: In a solid, the particles are very closely packed, in a regular pattern in most solids (crystalline solids); particles are also very closely packed in non-crystalline solids.

mcqs.q: The particles of a solid possess only:
mcqs.why: The particles of a solid can vibrate only about their equilibrium position and cannot make any translation or rotation, so the particles of a solid possess only vibrational kinetic energy.

mcqs.q: A solid has a definite shape and a definite volume because:
options: Its particles are far apart from each other
Its particles move freely in all directions
It has no forces acting between its particles
Strong forces of attraction hold its particles close together
mcqs.why: Strong forces of attraction hold the particles of a solid close together, and the particles can only vibrate about their equilibrium positions, so a solid keeps a definite shape and volume and has a high density.

mcqs.q: A solid cannot be compressed further because:
options: Its particles are already very closely packed, held close together by strong forces of attraction
It is too heavy to squeeze
Its particles are moving too fast
mcqs.why: The particles of a solid are very closely packed and strong forces of attraction hold the particles close together, so a solid cannot be further compressed.

mcqs.q: When a solid is heated until it melts, the binding force between its particles:
options: Changes into a force of repulsion
mcqs.why: When a solid is heated it melts into its liquid form: on heating, the binding force between the particles of the solid becomes slightly weak.

mcqs.q: A liquid has a definite volume but no definite shape because:
options: Its particles are locked in a regular pattern
Its particles have no attraction between them at all
Its particles can move freely within the container but stay confined to its boundary, so the liquid takes the shape of its container
Its particles are separated as widely as those of a gas
mcqs.why: The particles of a liquid are arranged randomly; they can move freely from one part of the liquid to another but are confined to the boundary of the container, so a liquid has a definite volume, takes the shape of its container, and can flow.

mcqs.q: The particles of a liquid possess:
mcqs.why: A liquid possesses translational and vibrational kinetic energies: its particles can move from one part of the liquid to another and can also vibrate, unlike the particles of a solid, which only vibrate.

mcqs.q: The density of most liquids is less than that of solids (except mercury) because:
options: Liquid particles are heavier than solid particles
The separation between the particles of a liquid is large compared to a solid
Liquid particles attract each other more strongly than solid particles
mcqs.why: In a liquid, the separation between two particles is large compared to a solid, and for this reason the density of most liquids (except mercury) is less than that of solids.

mcqs.q: The pressure of a gas is produced by:
options: Collisions of the gas particles with one another and with the walls of the container
The attraction between the gas particles
mcqs.why: The particles of a gas often collide with one another and with the walls of the container; the forces exerted by the particles during these collisions produce the pressure of the gas.

mcqs.q: A gas can be compressed, unlike a solid or a liquid, because:
options: Its particles attract each other strongly
The separation between its particles is quite large
mcqs.why: As the separation between the particles of a gas is quite large, the particles can be pushed closer together, so a gas can be compressed; gas particles do not occupy a fixed volume and quickly fill any available space.
